parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no documented border/document friction, no documented anti-trans violence pattern and no documented facility or custody rule reaching visitors. The operative negatives are a documented state posture: a 2024 cabinet direction and a ministry committee drafting a national ban on LGBTQIA+ advocacy and promotion, framed as contrary to constitutional and religious values, plus the absence of any anti-discrimination law and a demonstrated failure of protection machinery (Family Protection Act excludes same-sex partners; one prosecuted violence case ever). Countervailing: decriminalised same-sex conduct and prosecutorial guidance treating anti-GI hostility as aggravating. This is documented social/state hostility with thin, largely unexercised recourse — Elevated Risk, above regimes with actual entry or custodial exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented trans-specific border, marker-mismatch or secondary-screening practice; enforcement against visibly trans arrivals unknown.
entry_documents.interaction: Absence of documented friction in a reasonably reported jurisdiction is mildly positive but does not establish safety at the border.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented detention, custody-placement or investigation practice aimed at trans visitors; penal-code routes are the only avenue for partner violence.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Thin record; no evidence that identity checks escalate to custody, and no evidence they do not.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented bathroom, ward, shelter or facility-access rule applied by birth sex to visitors.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facilities exposure is undocumented rather than shown present; weigh as an open question, not as an offset.

care_services.exposure: No general anti-discrimination law covering services; nothing documented on refusal of care or lodging to trans visitors.
care_services.protection: Only narrow carve-outs (Teaching Service Act; Harmful Digital Communications Act) reach sexual orientation, not services generally.
care_services.interaction: Lawful discrimination in service settings is unprohibited, leaving visitors without recourse if refused, but no refusal is documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2024 council-of-ministers direction targeting LGBTQIA+ activities; ministry committee drafting a national ban on advocacy and promotion, framing the community as contrary to constitutional, religious and regional values.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Prosecution Policy 2003 and Prosecutors Code 2017 direct prosecutors to disregard sexual preference and treat GI/SO hostility as aggravating.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Suspicion attaches to public promotion, which a visibly trans visitor may be read as embodying; prosecutors' guidance is paper-only and rarely invoked.

minors_guardians.exposure: Nothing documented on trans minors, school placement, guardianship or family travel; conservative social climate is the only signal.
minors_guardians.interaction: Unknown; a family travelling with a gender-nonconforming minor faces an unevidenced but unsupported environment.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented anti-trans violence against visitors; only one prosecuted violence-against-lesbians case (2016) and a near-invisible LGBTI court presence.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Prosecutorial guidance treats bias motive as weighing toward prosecution; state signed the 2011 UN joint statement on SOGI violence.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Protection machinery exists on paper but the record shows it is almost never invoked, weakening its practical value.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination statute; Family Protection Act 2008 gives same-sex partners no protection; whether the advocacy-ban committee has produced enforceable policy, its legal form, and whether the marriage amendment touches documents are unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Penal-code complaints and consular channels only; court access undocumented for LGBTI claimants.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unanswered questions are not themselves exposure, but the documented gaps leave a victim with no realistic civil remedy.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra operates an explicit visitor register barring trans arrivals, with routine refusal of entry. This dossier documents no entry-denial mechanism or screening regime at all, so it sits clearly above that anchor, though its hostile state rhetoric and absent remedies keep it well below neutral.

Kestrel Isles documents recurring secondary screening, luggage searches and discretionary refused admission for document/presentation divergence. Here border friction is entirely undocumented, placing this jurisdiction above that anchor; but Kestrel's harm is administrative and remediable, whereas this dossier's state advocacy ban signals deeper institutional hostility, narrowing the gap.

Meridia has trained border officers, written reasons, counsel access and a tribunal that grants compensation. This dossier has no anti-discrimination law, no functioning LGBTI court presence, and a government drafting a ban on advocacy, so it sits materially below that anchor.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller's exposure here is not a statute, a checkpoint or a cell — none is documented — but an institutional climate: a 2024 executive direction framing LGBTQIA+ activity as contrary to national and religious values, a committee drafting a ban on advocacy and promotion, and the absence of any anti-discrimination guarantee, with the one protection (prosecutorial bias guidance) barely invoked. A visibly trans adult travelling alone likely meets curiosity and conservative disapproval rather than arrest; a family with a gender-nonconforming minor has no documented support and no clear recourse. Discrimination is lawful but not documented as practiced. This is documented hostility with thin remedy — Elevated Risk, short of regimes imposing actual entry or custodial exposure.
